chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who is an elderly shaykh or ill, and fears the pressure of the people and their crowding: may he enter into ihram for hajj and go out to Minā before the Day of Tarwiyah? He said: Yes. I said: Then may a healthy man go out seeking a place or seeking comfort thereby? He said: No. I said: May he go early by one day? He said: Yes. I said: By two days? He said: Yes. I said: By three? He said: Yes. I said: More than that? He said: No.

key_terms.شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا: an elderly man of advanced age
key_terms.ضِغَاطَ النَّاسِ: the pressing and pressure caused by people
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the ritual site near Makkah visited during hajj
key_terms.يَتَعَجَّلُ: goes earlier or advances ahead of the usual time
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the Day of Tarwiyah, the eighth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah

ai.seo_question: How many days before the Day of Tarwiyah may one go out to Minā according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the time of departing to Minā before the Day of Tarwiyah during hajj. It permits early departure for an elderly or ill person who fears crowding, and for a healthy person it allows advancing by up to three days, but not more.
